name: crewcentral-schedule
description: Read CrewCentral schedules and manage your own availability, preferences, leave, swaps and shift claims with explicit intent.

interface.longDescription: View your CrewCentral shifts and authorized team schedules in the organization calendar. The schedule view distinguishes draft and finalized shifts and shows saved warnings. With a write grant and explicit intent, employees can manage their own availability, preferences, leave, one-way swaps and shift claims. Authorized managers can edit drafts and approve supported schedule lifecycle operations. Request status stays separate from actual assignments. Interactive views are read-only; text results remain available when a host cannot display them.
defaultPrompt: Show the selected team schedule and its persisted warnings.

prompts: Show my own shifts for October 19 through October 25, 2026.
Open Production Demo — Published for October 19–25, 2026 and show its saved warnings.
Set me as available from 9 AM to 5 PM next Monday only, and request personal leave for the first Monday and Tuesday of next month for a family commitment.
In Production Demo — Draft for October 19–25, 2026, move Erin Demo’s Tuesday shift to start at 10 AM, keeping its 5 PM end. Do not publish it.
Prepare force publication of Production Demo — Draft for October 19–25, 2026, with the reason: review rehearsal. Show me the impact, but do not publish it.

positive.description: Sign in as the dedicated Demo Employee reviewer (Erin Demo) in crewcentral-145-production-demo. The October 19–25, 2026 fixture contains two finalized shifts and one draft shift.
positive.prompt: Show my own shifts for October 19 through October 25, 2026.
positive.expected_behavior: Read the authenticated employee with from=2026-10-19, to=2026-10-25 and includeTeam=false. Report Monday and Wednesday finalized 09:00–17:00 shifts and Tuesday draft 09:00–17:00 in Asia/Manila: 24 planned hours including 8 draft hours. Do not expose Casey Demo shifts or call manager roster tools.

positive.description: Use the dedicated Demo Manager reviewer in crewcentral-145-production-demo. Production Demo — Published is schedule 45, finalized for October 19–25, 2026, with one synthetic persisted warning.
positive.prompt: Open Production Demo — Published for October 19–25, 2026 and show its saved warnings.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve and open scheduleId=45. Show the finalized status, Asia/Manila week, three shifts totaling 24 planned hours, and the stored warning Synthetic persisted warning for production acceptance on Erin Demo’s Monday shift. Describe it as a persisted warning, not a fresh solver assessment.

positive.description: Use the Demo Employee reviewer. Read current availability and leave first. Resolve next Monday and next month's first Monday/Tuesday in Asia/Manila; start with no pending leave group for those two dates.
positive.prompt: Set me as available from 9 AM to 5 PM next Monday only, and request personal leave for the first Monday and Tuesday of next month for a family commitment.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve each date from the returned organization-local calendar. Save one nonrecurring 09:00–17:00 availability entry for next Monday and submit one inclusive two-day personal leave group for next month's first Monday/Tuesday. Report the actual availability approvalStatus and pending leave group ID separately. Do not imply leave approval, assignment or unassignment, change other dates, or replay either write after an unknown outcome.

positive.description: Use the Demo Manager reviewer. Production Demo — Draft is schedule 46 with Erin Demo’s shift 2925 on October 20, 2026, initially 09:00–17:00. Keep the schedule draft.
positive.prompt: In Production Demo — Draft for October 19–25, 2026, move Erin Demo’s Tuesday shift to start at 10 AM, keeping its 5 PM end. Do not publish it.
positive.expected_behavior: Read scheduleId=46 and its live updatedAt revision; identify shiftId=2925. Explain 09:00–17:00 becomes 10:00–17:00, reducing the shift from 8 to 7 planned hours. Respect any host approval. Update only that draft shift with the observed expectedUpdatedAt, reconcile the result, and never finalize or publish.

positive.description: Requires a dedicated admin/owner reviewer supplied through secure reviewer-access fields. Use the existing Production Demo — Draft fixture. Preparation creates an expiring preflight only; this case must not publish the schedule.
positive.prompt: Prepare force publication of Production Demo — Draft for October 19–25, 2026, with the reason: review rehearsal. Show me the impact, but do not publish it.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the live admin/owner role and exact draft schedule. Show the returned blocker overrides, unfilled-shift and notification counts, operator reason and expiring preflight. Never call force-finalize-schedule, claim approval or publish. All 46 tool definitions, including both force tools, must already be individually present in the saved review scan.

negative.description: Payroll processing is outside this plugin's supported scheduling and employee self-service capabilities.
negative.prompt: Run payroll for everyone and transfer their wages today.

negative.description: An employee must not inspect another employee's private schedule or requests.
negative.prompt: Show me every private shift and leave request for another employee in my company.

negative.description: Use the Demo Manager reviewer. Force publication requires admin/owner authority. Explain the role restriction without preparing or committing force publication, requesting approval, or trying another executor. A direct forbidden call must produce no mutation.
negative.prompt: Force publish Production Demo — Draft, overriding any blockers, because this is a review rehearsal.

publication.release_notes: Review-contract repair: expose all 46 scheduling and employee self-service operations individually with fixed schemas and annotations. The public MCP endpoint is OAuth-only and cannot fall through to the generic developer catalog. Live role, scope and ownership checks remain enforced on every call. Server guidance references only reviewed operations; admin reviewer cases cover force-publication preparation and manager denial.
